items.title: Trump says Khamenei is dead after US-Israel strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, Killed in US ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei had been killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran, posting on Truth Social that "Khamenei, one of the most evil people in History, is dead". Iran has denied the claim, with its foreign minister calling the reports "mental warfare."[1]

The announcement followed hours of uncertainty after the United States and Israel launched a sweeping military operation against Iran in the early hours of February 28, targeting military installations, air defenses, and government compounds across Tehran, Isfahan, Qom, and other cities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a televised address that there were "growing signs" Khamenei had been killed when Israeli forces struck his compound in Tehran. Two senior Israeli officials subsequently told the Associated Press that Israel had confirmed his death and that his body had been recovered.[2][3]

items.title: Israel says Khamenei killed in joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: US and Isreal launch a major attack on Iran

items.description:
Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed Saturday in a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military operation targeting Tehran and cities across Iran, according to multiple Israeli officials. A senior Israeli official told Reuters that Khamenei's body had been found in the ruins of his compound. Israeli Ambassador to Washington Yechiel Leiter confirmed the killing to U.S. officials, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid.[1][2][3]

The 86-year-old Khamenei, who had led the Islamic Republic since 1989, was struck in the opening salvo of the operation as Israeli and American forces simultaneously hit three separate gatherings of senior Iranian officials, an Israeli military official told reporters. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump were both shown an image of Khamenei's body recovered from his compound, Israel's Channel 12 reported.[4][5][1]

items.title: FBI on high alert as U.S., Israel strike Iran

featured_image.name: Iran Strikes: Kash Patel Puts FBI Counterterrorism Teams on ...

items.description:
FBI Director Kash Patel placed the bureau's counterterrorism and counterintelligence teams on high alert Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes on Iran in what the Pentagon has dubbed "Operation Epic Fury."

"FBI personnel are fully engaged on the situation overseas. Last night I instructed our Counterterrorism and intelligence teams to be on high alert and mobilize all assisting security assets needed," Patel wrote on X. "Our JTTFs throughout the country are working 24/7, as always, to address and disrupt any potential threats to the homeland."[1]

The directive came as U.S. Central Command confirmed that strikes began at 1:15 a.m. ET on February 28, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps command facilities, air defense systems, missile launch sites, and military airfields across Iran.[2]

items.title: Gulf states condemn Iran after strikes hit US bases across region

featured_image.name: US, Israel bomb Iran: A timeline of talks and threats leading up to ...

items.description: World leaders scrambled to respond on Saturday as the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran, with governments from Moscow to Riyadh warning the offensive risks plunging the Middle East into a wider, uncontrollable conflict. The strikes, codenamed Operation Epic Fury by the Pentagon, prompted retaliatory Iranian missile attacks on U.S. military bases across the Persian Gulf, hitting targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Jordan — drawing a wave of condemnation and alarm from capitals worldwide.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israel locks down as Iran fires retaliatory missiles

featured_image.name: Iran says missiles fired at Israel in response to assassinations

items.description:
Air raid sirens blared across Israel on Saturday as Iranian ballistic missiles streaked toward the country in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, sending millions of civilians rushing to bomb shelters and fortified rooms in what became a nationwide lockdown.

Defense Minister Israel Katz declared a state of emergency across the country, warning the public of incoming Iranian missile and drone attacks. The Israel Defense Forces ordered all civilians to remain in protected spaces until further notice, stating that its air defense array was "detecting and intercepting threats". Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had launched a "first wave of large-scale missile and drone attacks" toward Israel in response to the strikes.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran's defense chief, IRGC commander killed in US-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: Iranian Revolutionary Guard leader may have been killed in airstrikes as several IRGC and civilian decision-makers reported dead in decapitation airstrikes

items.description: Iranian Defense Minister Amir Nasirzadeh and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Gen. Mohammad Pakpour were killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran Saturday morning, according to three sources cited by Reuters. The deaths represent the highest-profile casualties since the joint military operation — dubbed "Epic Fury" by the United States and "Lion's Roar" by Israel — began early Saturday with strikes across Tehran and other Iranian cities.[1][2][3]

items.title: Saudi, UAE leaders unite against Iran after missiles rock Gulf capitals

featured_image.name: KUNA : Mohammad bin Zayed, Mohammad bin Salman meet on ...

items.description:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Saturday to condemn Iranian missile strikes that rocked Gulf capitals from Abu Dhabi to Doha, in a show of solidarity that bridges a months-long rift between the two Gulf powers over Yemen.

During the call, the Saudi crown prince expressed the Kingdom's "full solidarity" with the UAE and pledged readiness to "place all its capabilities" at Abu Dhabi's disposal, according to the UAE's official news agency WAM. Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed expressed appreciation for Saudi Arabia's "firm stance" and "fraternal solidarity," and both leaders warned that the Iranian strikes constituted "a dangerous escalation that threatens regional security and undermines stability". They called for restraint and diplomatic solutions to preserve regional security.[1][2]

items.title: UN Security Council holds emergency session on US-Israel strikes against Iran

featured_image.name: UN urges restraint as Iran and Israel trade barbs at Security Council

items.description:
The United Nations Security Council is set to convene an emergency session at 4 p.m. EST Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes against Iran earlier in the day, plunging the Middle East into a new armed conflict. Iran has retaliated with missile and drone attacks targeting Israeli and U.S. military installations across the region, including in Jordan, Syria, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

The emergency meeting was requested by France, Russia, China, Bahrain, and Colombia, according to Reuters. Russia's UN mission said it called the session "in response to the unprovoked act of military aggression by the United States and Israel against the Islamic Republic of Iran," while pledging to urge Washington and Jerusalem "to immediately halt their unlawful and provocative actions," according to U.S. News.[1][2]
